Formulation:  
Middle-aged male with a recent onset (1 week) of mild swelling and warmth over the left elbow without pain or loss of function. Past history of osteoarthritis may predispose to periarticular inflammation such as bursitis. Physical exam supports likely olecranon bursitis; no signs of acute infection currently. Differential diagnosis includes early septic bursitis, gout, or other inflammatory arthropathies. Blood tests planned for inflammatory markers, autoimmune screening, and gout profile to clarify cause. Psychosocial factors minimal; patient physically active and has good insight into condition and treatment plan. Early follow-up arranged to monitor progress and manage worsening symptoms if they occur.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Olecranon bursitis  
- Patient Goal(s): Resolution of swelling and discomfort, return to normal elbow function without complications  
- Clinical Goal(s): Confirm diagnosis; exclude infection and other inflammatory causes via blood tests; manage symptoms with anti-inflammatory medication  
- Actions (Patient): Take Ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food as advised; complete blood tests as arranged; monitor elbow for worsening symptoms, especially increased redness, pain, or swelling  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Arrange and send blood test forms for inflammatory markers, infection screen, autoimmune antibodies, and gout profile; review blood test results; arrange follow-up appointment (in-person or remote) after investigations; provide advice on emergency signs and when to seek urgent care  

Secondary Problem: Septic bursitis (to monitor/rule out)  
- Patient Goal(s): Avoid progression to infection, remain aware of signs of worsening condition  
- Clinical Goal(s): Early identification of infection signs; timely intervention if septic bursitis develops  
- Actions (Patient): Seek immediate medical attention if elbow becomes very red, extremely painful, or swelling worsens; utilize video or face-to-face consultation if symptoms worsen  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Educate patient regarding emergency signs; triage promptly if signs develop  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:  
- Education Given: Yes  
- Topics Covered: Nature of bursitis, use of anti-inflammatory medication, importance of blood tests, signs of potential infection/septic arthritis requiring urgent care  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased redness, spreading erythema, severe pain, fever, decreased range of motion  
- Coping Strategies: Regular monitoring of symptoms; maintaining physical activity within comfort limits; prompt communication with healthcare provider if symptoms worsen  

Consent, Coordination & Review:  
- Patient Consent to Plan: Implied by agreement in consultation (not explicitly documented)  
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded  
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None  
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable  
- Review Date: Within approximately 1 week after blood test completion (six days anticipated for results)  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)  
- Olecranon bursitis: High likelihood based on localized swelling, warmth, no trauma, normal joint function, and GP clinical impression.  
- Septic bursitis: Medium likelihood; possible early infection considered but unlikely due to lack of redness, pain, or systemic symptoms. Requires monitoring.  
- Gout or crystal arthropathy: Medium likelihood; acute monoarticular swelling considered, blood tests planned to exclude this cause.
